course.title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
course.summary: This course covers asymptotic notations, recurrences, algorithmic design paradigms (divide-and-conquer, greedy, dynamic programming), graph algorithms, complexity hierarchies, and NP-completeness reductions.

course_outcomes.statement: Explain asymptotic complexity notations, recurrence relations, and algorithmic efficiency models across best, average, and worst-case bounds.
Apply divide-and-conquer, greedy selection, and dynamic programming techniques to solve constrained algorithmic optimization problems.
Analyze minimum spanning tree, shortest path, and maximum network flow algorithms on sparse and dense graph topologies.
Differentiate polynomial vs non-deterministic polynomial problem classes (P, NP, NP-Complete) using formal reduction proofs.
Evaluate randomized and approximation heuristics for computationally intractable NP-hard combinatorial bottlenecks.
Design branch-and-bound and state-space search architectures for high-dimensional computational decision systems.

units.title: Introduction & Asymptotic Analysis
units.topics: Order Notation (O, Omega, Theta), Master Theorem, Substitution Method, Recursion Tree, Recurrences, Amortized Analysis.

units.title: Divide & Conquer and Greedy Paradigms
units.topics: Strassen Matrix Multiplication, Convex Hull, Greedy Choice Property, Optimal Substructure, Fractional Knapsack, Huffman Coding.

units.title: Dynamic Programming & Graph Algorithms
units.topics: Matrix Chain Multiplication, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), 0/1 Knapsack, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, Ford-Fulkerson.

units.title: Tractability & NP-Completeness
units.topics: Deterministic vs Non-deterministic Turing Machines, Polynomial Reductions, Cook-Levin Theorem, Satisfiability (3-SAT), Clique, Vertex Cover.

units.title: Approximation, Randomized & Branch-and-Bound
units.topics: Approximation Ratio, Vertex Cover 2-Approximation, Metric TSP, Random Treaps, Quickselect, Branch and Bound LC-Search, 15-Puzzle Problem.
